detail.abstract: Indonesia channels more than IDR 70 trillion annually through village fiscal transfers to 75,265 village governments without a nationally standardized instrument for measuring the economic productivity of recipient units. Existing performance indices (the Village Development Index [IDM], SDGs Desa, and Indeks Desa) evaluate administrative compliance and service delivery; none measures village economic output. This paper introduces the Village Productivity Index (VPI/IPD), a composite index operationalizing the productive territorial unit (PTU) framework to assess rural economic productivity across five weighted dimensions: primary sector output (25%), economic diversification (20%), labor productivity (20%), Dana Desa fiscal return (20%), and market integration (15%). Theoretically, the VPI integrates Pritchett, Woolcock, and Andrews's (2013) isomorphic mimicry framework with North's (1990) institutional economics and OECD Rural Policy 3.0. Methodologically, the index employs Winsorized normalization at national P5/P95 percentiles and a three-year backward-moving average for the fiscal return dimension. A stratified pilot empirical analysis on 1,200 villages across six provinces demonstrates meaningful inter-village discrimination (mean VPI = 51.3, SD = 14.7; range 18.4-82.6) and preliminary predictive validity (r = 0.41 with district PDRB per capita, p < 0.001). Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis (n = 10,000) confirms classification stability for 78.4% of villages. AHP expert elicitation (n = 18 specialists) yields weights statistically indistinguishable from the proposed scheme. Integration of VPI into Dana Desa allocation formulae under UU HKPD No. 1 Tahun 2022 could redirect IDR 7-10 trillion annually to villages with demonstrated productive performance, with a conservatively simulated aggregate output effect of IDR 3.2-5.8 trillion annually under explicitly stated assumptions and a correlation-based, non-causal model.

title: Beyond Capabilities: Agency Continuity, the Provident Approach, and What the Human Development Index Cannot See
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Beyond Capabilities: Agency Continuity, the Provident Approach, and What the Human Development Index Cannot See
detail.abstract: Can a society register very high human development while eroding the structural conditions that make comparable agency possible for its successors? This article argues that capability evaluation and the Human Development Index do not directly measure that question, because their evaluative object is the person's present opportunity set rather than the reproducibility of the systems on which any opportunity set depends. It introduces the Provident Approach, an evaluative orientation concerned with agency continuity: the reliable reproduction, across generations, of the biological, demographic, institutional, cognitive, monetary, and formative conditions of meaningful human action. It advances an analytic-priority claim: capability assessment presupposes a structural substrate whose continuity must be evaluated at a distinct level, with a distinct evaluand. The argument is developed through four backcasting cases, a capability-continuity typology, and a preliminary measurement architecture, the Providence Value Unit, whose weighted geometric aggregation expresses non-substitutability among structural pillarsextending a logic the human development community adopted in the 2010 revision of the HDI. The relationship proposed is complementary: as the HDI added human dimensions to the measurement of economies, the Provident Approach adds structural-reproductive dimensions to the measurement of human development.

title: Governance Beyond Hierarchy: Validation of the 2026 Power Dynamics Scale (PDS-26) for Algorithmic and Remote Leadership
affiliations: Walden University

detail.title: Governance Beyond Hierarchy: Validation of the 2026 Power Dynamics Scale (PDS-26) for Algorithmic and Remote Leadership
detail.abstract: The interplay among Organizational Power, Resource Dependency, Ideology, Cognitive Authority, and Emergent Brokers is fundamentally reshaping the governance landscape of 2026. This study introduces and validates the 2026 Power Dynamics Scale (PDS-26), a specialized instrument designed to measure how the transition from physical to digital presence affects managerial control and leadership legitimacy. Grounded in Upper Echelons Theory and New Institutionalism, the research examines the "Presence Paradox" in remote work and the tension between AI-driven algorithmic logic and seasoned human intuition. A quantitative content validation study with an elite panel of 10 Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) established the PDS-26's content and face validity across diverse industry contexts. By assessing how decentralized models and automated protocols shift traditional "locations of power," the study identifies mechanisms, such as "Safety Traps" and "Algorithmic Subjectivity," that intermediaries use to maintain brokerage power. The resulting framework provides a validated methodological foundation for sustaining organizational governance and effectiveness in an increasingly technologyaugmented, multi-generational corporate environment.

title: Manufacturing Demand Forecasting using Data Science: An EDA-Driven Approach on Smart Manufacturing IoT-Cloud Monitoring Dataset
affiliations: and Sinhgad Institute of Management, Pune

detail.title: Manufacturing Demand Forecasting using Data Science: An EDA-Driven Approach on Smart Manufacturing IoT-Cloud Monitoring Dataset
detail.abstract: Detecting equipment failure before it happens is one of the biggest problems faced by manufacturing plants today. In this paper, we look at how machine learning can be used to spot unusual behaviour in industrial machines using sensor data collected from the Smart Manufacturing IoT-Cloud Monitoring Dataset. The dataset has 1,00,000 sensor readings from 50 machines, recorded over 69 days from January 2025 to March 2025. It covers five sensor types-temperature, vibration, humidity, pressure, and energy consumption-along with information like machine status, anomaly flags, downtime risk, and predicted remaining life. We tested three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest. Our analysis found that about 8.92% of sensor readings were flagged as anomalies. Among all sensors, temperature turned out to be the most useful in spotting problems, with a feature importance score of 0.7522. The Random Forest model gave the best results with 99.99% accuracy, 99.89% precision, and a 99.94% F1-score. This work shows that ensemble methods can work very well for catching machine faults in real time and can serve as a strong base for building smarter maintenance and production systems.

title: Why I'm Uncertain About 'Speech Certainty': A Response to Austin & Levy

detail.title: Why I'm Uncertain About 'Speech Certainty': A Response to Austin & Levy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

contentType.other: This is a paper that was submitted to Stanford Law Review Online and made it to the final round but was subsequently rejected. I am currently submitting it to other journals.

detail.abstract:
Sometimes the most elegant solution is the simplest. And indeed, that appears to be the case with Austin & Levy’s ‘Speech Certainty.’ As courts are increasingly asked to adjudicate whether machine learning (ML) output should receive First Amendment protections, the authors offer an epiphany. “Speech,” they explain, “is characterized by speech certainty when the speech can be identified with certainty by the speaker at the moment it is spoken.” Speech lacking that quality also lacks First Amendment protection. And, because ML output lacks ‘certainty’, the First Amendment’s protections do not attach.

The theory is elegant. It provides a “key to history” that is almost Newtonian in origin. It feels natural that only a speaker who “knew for certain what she said when she said it” is the essential nature of speech. So much so, that once you discover ‘speech certainty,’ it appears everywhere in the First Amendment’s text, history, and purpose. But its elegance hides its flaws. ‘Speech Certainty’ simply confirms a solution, and with it, disenfranchises an entire category of already vulnerable individuals.

I am uncertain about Speech Certainty for two reasons. First, Austin & Levy’s theory presupposes itself. Instead of developing ‘speech certainty’ from the First Amendment’s text, history, and purpose, the authors simply arrive at it and purport to show how history and tradition compel its acceptance. Second, the theory should give us pause. In proposing their solution, based on 18th century notions of “speech,” the authors overlook the consequence that it denies First Amendment protections to cognitively impaired persons. People who, at the Founding, were not considered ‘certain’ of anything.

There may be a simpler solution. ML output shouldn’t receive First Amendment protections at the moment of generation because it is not human. The Supreme Court has never protected the speech of non-humans absent some connection to a user or receiver. The same should apply to machine output. This preserves avenues for AI safety regulation while preserving the rights of those with cognitive impairments.

title: All that Glitters is not a DMA Review
affiliations: University Villanueva

detail.title: All that Glitters is not a DMA Review
detail.abstract: The European Commission's review report claims the regulation has broadly succeeded in making digital markets fairer and more contestable, yet this assessment rests on selectively highlighted achievements while systematically omitting enforcement shortcomings. Although positive outcomes are documented, the review glosses over persistent self-preferencing, unresolved compliance disputes, and the departure of business users from DMA-opened markets. Critically, the report fails to adequately address the DMA's fragmentation of the internal market, arising from divergent national competition law applications, private enforcement proceedings across Member States, and gatekeepers' own compliance strategies. Enforcement procedural irregularities limited third-party participation, and the unresolved treatment of AI and cloud services under the regulation's scope further undermine the review's optimistic conclusions. The article argues that regulatory resilience requires honest accounting of what has not worked, a standard the Commission's review conspicuously fails to meet.

title:
Strategic Finance Under Environmental Turbulence: 
The Sarikhan Strategic Finance Posture Model

detail.title:
Strategic Finance Under Environmental Turbulence: 
The Sarikhan Strategic Finance Posture Model

declarations.ethicsApproval: This conceptual article does not involve human subjects research, primary data collection, identifiable private information, or intervention with participants. Therefore, institutional ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding involved.

detail.abstract:
Environmental turbulence challenges firms to align strategy, capability, and financial decision-
making with changing external conditions. Traditional strategic management models emphasize
the need to match strategic aggressiveness to the level of environmental turbulence. However,
financial strategy is often treated as a supporting function rather than as a direct dimension of
strategic posture. This article introduces the Sarikhan Strategic Finance Posture Model as an
extension of strategic aggressiveness alignment. The model argues that firms must align their
financial posture with environmental turbulence in the same way they align innovation and
marketing aggressiveness. Strategic Finance is conceptualized in terms of multiple attributes,
including capital structure posture, investment posture, budgeting logic, financial risk posture,
liquidity posture, technology and innovation financing, growth financing, cost-of-capital
orientation, financing flexibility, and the strategic role of finance. A questionnaire is developed
to assess Strategic Finance Aggressiveness Level across five stages: maintenance-focused,
defensive, balanced, flexible, and transformational. The article also proposes a gap-diagnosis
method that compares the internally assessed Strategic Finance posture with the externally
assessed Environmental Turbulence Level. The resulting Strategic Finance Gap may help top
management, CFOs, researchers, and consultants identify whether a firm’s financial posture is
under-aggressive, aligned, or over-aggressive relative to its environment. The article contributes
to strategic management and strategic finance by positioning finance as an active strategic
posture dimension rather than merely a control, reporting, or resource-allocation function.

title: The Party's Over: How the Bitcoin ETF Killed Crypto's Cool Factor
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: The Party's Over: How the Bitcoin ETF Killed Crypto's Cool Factor
detail.abstract: This paper documents a structural break in the risk return characteristics and cultural relevance of cryptocurrencies following the approval of the first spot Bitcoin ETF on January 10, 2024. Using daily price data from January 2021 to June 2026, we compare pre ETF and post ETF performance metrics, betas, and event study cumulative abnormal returns for Bitcoin, Dogecoin, and Ethereum relative to the S&P 500 and gold. We then introduce two independent measures of public interest, Google Trends and Wikipedia page views, to test the hypothesis that Bitcoin lost its cultural "coolness" after institutionalization. The findings are striking. Dogecoin, the quintessential speculative asset, saw its Sharpe ratio collapse from 0.30 pre ETF to 0.01 post ETF, while its annualized return fell from 63.17% to 2.82%. Google search interest for Dogecoin declined 63.1% and its Wikipedia page views collapsed 75.9%. Searches for "how to buy Bitcoin," a proxy for new retail entrants, declined 22.7%. In contrast, general "cryptocurrency" interest fell 47.5%, while Bitcoin maintained a stable Sharpe ratio and saw its beta relative to the S&P 500 decline from 1.33 to 1.11. An event study reveals that the Trump 2024 election produced a +47.37% cumulative abnormal return for Dogecoin, but this proved temporary. The MSTR sale in May 2026, Michael Saylor's first Bitcoin sale since 2022, generated a-6.56% abnormal return for Bitcoin. These results support the thesis that ETF approval marked a cultural as well as financial regime shift, as retail speculative energy exited the crypto market and Bitcoin moved toward more of a diversifier role.

title: Unpacking the Green Innovation Slowdown
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong and HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Unpacking the Green Innovation Slowdown
detail.abstract: Despite escalating climate concerns and intensifying policy support, aggregate green innovation has puzzlingly slowed since 2010 across various OECD countries. Using U.S. patent data, we document that green innovation is concentrated among firms with information and communication technology (ICT) capabilities and that these firms primarily drive the post-2010 stagnation. To rationalize these facts, we develop and estimate a general equilibrium model featuring endogenous technology-class selection, directed innovation, and firm dynamics. In the model, ICT firms possess a comparative advantage in green innovation through lower innovation costs. Our model highlights a fundamental policy trade-off: ICT-targeted green subsidies are more efficient than uniform subsidies when dirty innovation is relatively costly, while the reverse holds when dirty innovation is cheap, due to general-equilibrium crowd-out effects. Quantitatively, we find that the ICT innovation slowdown is the primary catalyst for the slowdown in green innovation, overshadowing the effects of falling fossil-energy prices and shifts in entrant composition. Policy counterfactuals reveal that an ICT-targeted subsidy yields a higher consumption-to-subsidy multiplier than a uniform subsidy, both before and during the green innovation slowdown. Our results also provide an economic rationale for the twin-transition agenda: effective climate innovation policy must account for heterogeneity in firms' digital capabilities because the path to decarbonization is increasingly digital.

title: Beyond Fitness Landscapes: Constructibility as a Constraint on Evolutionary Trajectories
affiliations: Azerbaijan Technical University and

detail.title: Beyond Fitness Landscapes: Constructibility as a Constraint on Evolutionary Trajectories
detail.abstract: We propose a new geometric language for evolutionary accessibility, introducing the Constructibility Landscape as a formal mathematical structure that characterizes which biological forms are reachable-not merely which are fittest. The central distinction of this framework is that fitness evaluates states, while constructibility evaluates trajectories. Formally, we define the constructibility landscape as a quadruple CL = (X, V, F, M_C(x_0, F)), where M_C(x_0, F) = Reach_F(X_V, x_0) is the dynamical reachability operator over the viable set X_V under evolutionary dynamics F. We prove that M_C is a positively Finvariant subset of X_V that is generically strictly smaller than the path-connected component of X_V-the gap between them constituting the set of evolutionarily inaccessible forms. We further prove that the classical fitness landscape is a projection of the constructibility landscape under the terminal-state evaluation map, making constructibility the more fundamental object. A separation theorem grounded in the Chow-Rashevsky controllability theorem establishes that constructibility coincides with topological viability only in the degenerate case of fully controllable evolutionary dynamics-a case no realistic biological system satisfies. We derive a three-layer evolutionary architecture (Constructibility → Viability → Selection), in which natural selection operates at the third layer alone. Within this framework, convergent evolution, developmental constraints, evolutionary lock-in, and missing biological forms all admit precise geometric characterizations. The framework connects naturally to viability theory, geometric control theory, and complex adaptive systems, and we conjecture that an analogous three-layer structure governs adaptive dynamics across biological, artificial, and institutional domains.

title: Proof of Stake Economy under Centralized Exchanges – A Mean Field Model
affiliations: Columbia University - Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research

detail.title: Proof of Stake Economy under Centralized Exchanges – A Mean Field Model
detail.abstract: We consider the interaction between centralized trading and decentralized Proof of Stake (PoS) blockchain ecosystems. Motivated by the increasing dominance of centralized exchanges and the institutionalization of crypto markets, we study how trading activities on centralized exchanges affect staking behavior, token allocation, and decentralization within a PoS blockchain. We formulate a continuous-time mean field model, where the miners simultaneously act as validators in the PoS protocol and traders in a centralized market with price impact. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the local well-posedness of the mean field system, and derive a semi-explicit characterization of the equilibrium trading strategy. Numerical results suggest that centralized trading activities may enhance staking participation, and promote decentralization of the staking distribution through market incentives. We also study the effects of transaction costs and token supply mechanisms on the equilibrium staking ratio and concentration profile. These results illustrate how market microstructure and centralized liquidity provision can exert significant influence on decentralized blockchain protocols.

title: Longtermism and Rule Consequentialism. A Tripartite Criticism

detail.title: Longtermism and Rule Consequentialism. A Tripartite Criticism
detail.abstract: This paper advances a criticism of longtermism by first arguing that rule consequentialism (RC) provides a particularly suitable normative framework for evaluating the large-scale, collective actions that longtermism requires. Building on recent developments in RC in response to the Ideal World Objection, the paper then shows that longtermism faces significant limitations in guiding the actions of individuals, institutions, and tech billionaires. For each of these categories of agents, longtermism proves liable to be self-defeating once one considers, respectively, compliance rates, acceptance rates, and transition barriers of the longtermist norms. Individual and institutional actions can produce long-term benefits only under conditions of high compliance and acceptance, which are unlikely for these norms. Regarding tech billionaires, we evaluate potential attempts to engineer the required acceptance rates by manipulating the socio-technical context. These attempts would introduce low transition barriers to conditions with low expected values, since the same tools being used by these agents could facilitate social engineering for harmful purposes.

title: A Defaultable-Commodity Framework for Compute Capacity Contracts
affiliations: and

detail.title: A Defaultable-Commodity Framework for Compute Capacity Contracts
detail.abstract: Reserved compute capacity is increasingly tradable amid surging AI-infrastructure investment: in large wholesale blocks and, more recently, through exchange-listed and cleared instruments. Yet pricing a compute capacity contract-a defaultable claim on a non-storable good that obsolesces on a known hardware cadence, sold by issuers that may fail in structurally distinct ways-still falls in the gap between standard commodity and credit finance. We develop a single-issuer pricing framework for this emerging asset class, adapting reduced-form credit intensity and Föllmer-Schweizer hedging to its defining features. The framework is closed-form under affine intensity and is exercised on an H100 forward through the H100→B200 transition.

title: On-Demand Service Zone Design for Energy-Constrained Spatial Queueing Systems
affiliations: , Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) - Antai College of Economics and Management, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University

detail.title: On-Demand Service Zone Design for Energy-Constrained Spatial Queueing Systems
detail.abstract: Electric service vehicles (ESVs), such as mobile chargers and drone-based service units, are becoming an important operational resource for on-demand service systems. Unlike conventional spatial servers, ESV operations are shaped by battery limits and recharging needs, which affect dispatch feasibility and spatial deployment decisions. We develop an energy-constrained hypercube spatial queueing model that embeds battery-state dynamics into the classical hypercube framework and uses a semi-Markov representation to estimate steady-state performance. We then formulate a joint location-zoning problem for station placement and service zone design. The resulting model is a large-scale mixed-integer nonlinear program, whose set partitioning reformulation has objective coefficients that are not available in closed form. We therefore develop a Branch-Price-and-Evaluation framework for set partitioning problems with externally computable column coefficients: upper-bounding surrogates guide pricing, and iterative exact evaluation updates the coefficients of active columns. Computational results show that explicit energy modeling significantly reduces false service promises and yields more credible planning decisions. They also reveal a load-dependent reversal in zoning: pooling is preferable under light demand, whereas tighter zoning becomes more profitable as demand increases. Over the tested range, profitability is driven more by zoning than by battery improvement, suggesting that managers should get service zone design right before investing in battery upgrades; this caution is reinforced by the counterintuitive finding that larger batteries may delay replenishment and reduce fleet readiness under sparse demand. These findings highlight a broader planning insight for energy-constrained mobile service systems: energy feasibility should be treated not merely as a matter of battery-capacity expansion, but as a design dimension that shapes service-zone configuration.

title: Joint Dynamic Pricing and Free Upgrades for Multiple Perishable Products
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU), Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST), City University of Hong Kong and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST)

detail.title: Joint Dynamic Pricing and Free Upgrades for Multiple Perishable Products
detail.abstract: Dynamic pricing and free upgrades are powerful mechanisms for managing demand and capacity when firms sell multiple perishable products. Dynamic pricing adjusts prices to steer demand across products, while free upgrades allow firms to satisfy demand for an unavailable lower-quality product using excess capacity of a higher-quality product. Although both practices are widely used in industries such as airlines, hotels, and retailing, prior research has largely studied them separately. This paper examines their joint role and evaluates when free upgrades create value within a dynamic pricing framework. We model customer utility as the sum of a quality-sensitive component and a base utility component, where base utility captures the intrinsic value of purchasing from the firm independent of product quality. Embedding this demand model into a dynamic pricing problem with multiple vertically differentiated, perishable products, we show that the value of free upgrades depends critically on base utility. In particular, free upgrades strictly increase expected revenue only when base utility is positive. When the base utility is common across products, we further show that free upgrades should be offered only to satisfy demand for the stocked-out lowest-quality product, using the closest available higher-quality inventory, and only when the marginal value of that higher-quality inventory is below the base utility. Thus, under dynamic pricing, upgrading is not a general substitution tool, but rather a targeted mechanism for expanding effective demand at the lowest tier. Building on these structural insights, we study a budget-constrained inventory planning problem under uniformly distributed consumer types. We develop fluid approximations of the dynamic revenue function and propose constant-factor approximation algorithms with provable performance guarantees. Numerical experiments quantify the revenue gains from free upgrades and show that the proposed inventory policies achieve near-optimal performance across a broad range of settings. Overall, our results clarify when free upgrades complement dynamic pricing and provide both managerial guidance and algorithmic tools for managing vertically differentiated, perishable products.

title: Decoding Xi Jinping: How Will China's Bureaucrats Interpret His Call for "Common Prosperity?"
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: Decoding Xi Jinping: How Will China's Bureaucrats Interpret His Call for "Common Prosperity?"
detail.abstract:
This is a preprint / author manuscript version of an essay published in Foreign Affairs. It is provided in text-only form and is not the publisher-formatted final version. The original publication is acknowledged and linked where available.

Xi Jinping's signature "common prosperity" campaign has frequently confounded foreign observers, investors, and policymakers. To clarify this ambiguity, Yuen Yuen Ang applies her framework of "directed improvisation"—a governance model in which top leadership issues overarching mandates while millions of bureaucrats devise locally tailored solutions—to decode Xi's foundational manifesto published in Qiushi, the Chinese Communist Party’s theoretical journal.

Through this lens, Ang identifies three distinct typologies of instruction embedded within Xi's text. "Red" directives establish firm boundaries, such as avoiding the rigid, quantitative target-setting seen in earlier poverty eradication campaigns. "Black" directives explicitly mandate specific actions, including the expansion of state-owned enterprises and the tightening of ideological control. Finally, "gray" directives remain deliberately ambiguous to foster local experimentation; most notably, Xi designates Zhejiang Province as a developmental template to be adapted, rather than rigidly copied, by other localities.

Ang conceptualizes the common prosperity initiative as an exercise in "Red Progressivism": a top-down mandate to rescue China from its Gilded Age of crony capitalism and usher in an era analogous to America's Progressive Era, though notably absent the grassroots democratic activism that drove U.S. reforms. Ultimately, Ang concludes that whether Xi can successfully navigate the fundamental tension between taming capitalist excesses and maintaining entrepreneurial vitality will depend entirely on how bureaucrats across the hierarchy interpret and execute his strategically open-ended vision.

title: Managing Countries: The Recipe for Leading a Nation to a Developed State

detail.title: Managing Countries: The Recipe for Leading a Nation to a Developed State

detail.abstract: Multiple theories on the development of countries are available, and every year several development rankings are published. Yet, no systematic or structured path for advancing a nation is evident. It is often assumed that the factors used in these rankings, along with governance indicators, can serve as a basis for planning development. However, there is neither uniformity in the factors employed across rankings nor any established theoretical interrelationship among them. This study proposes a development model that integrates diverse factors in a systematic manner, offering a step-by-step pathway for nations to achieve developed status. Fourteen development factors were selected from existing theories and various indices. These factors were analyzed using Interpretive Structural Modelling (ISM) and Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (TISM) methods to construct a comprehensive framework. The resulting model highlights two foundational requirements for development: controlling population growth and ensuring politics remain free from religious influence. These foundational elements drive other development factors, which ultimately lead to outcomes such as long and healthy lives, supported by linkage factors like economic and sustainable growth.

title: Neural Assortment Optimization
affiliations: , University of Chicago, Ohio State University (OSU), Clear Street, University of Texas at Austin - Department of Information, Risk, and Operations Management and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Neural Assortment Optimization
detail.abstract: Assortment optimization selects a subset of items to maximize expected revenue under a discrete choice model and is widely used in revenue management and online platforms. Its combinatorial nature creates a practical tension among generality, scalability, and provable guarantees: model-specific algorithms can be strong when their structural assumptions hold, but are hard to adapt across choice models; broadly applicable heuristics and learning-based methods scale to large instances but often come without near-optimality guarantees. We propose Neural Assortment Optimization (NAO), a choice-modelagnostic optimization framework that only requires an oracle that evaluates the expected revenue of a candidate assortment. NAO follows an "extend-particle search-round" pipeline: it constructs a tight continuous extension of the discrete objective, then optimizes a population of interacting particles using noisy subgradient descent, and finally rounds candidates back to discrete assortments. The particle objective admits a simple neural-network interpretation: each particle can be viewed as a hidden neuron, and an entropic-risk pooling layer emphasizes the best-performing candidates during optimization. We establish global convergence and near-optimality guarantees under mild conditions, and extend the method to cardinality constraints via a capacity-aware rolling-window construction. Experiments on challenging Mixed MNL and Nested Logit benchmarks show that NAO achieves near-optimal revenue with strong computational efficiency, consistently outperforming competitive heuristics and neural baselines and scaling well to large instances.

title: Fatigue Risk Management as a Hard Rostering Constraint for Crewing a Multi-Type Helicopter Emergency Medical Service

detail.abstract: This study models crew rostering for a multi-type helicopter emergency medical service (HEMS) fleet in which a fatigue risk management system (FRMS) acts as a hard assignment constraint. A pilot above a cumulative-load threshold is not rostered to a duty slot even when current on the type. It tests one hypothesis, H1, that rotational assignment under the FRMS maintains multi-type proficiency while reducing recurrent-training cost. A four-tier pilot categorisation (A-D) was defined against European flight-crew licensing and recency rules and a 24/48 duty cycle. The categories are built so that no pilot exceeds the legal limit on type combinations. Category A flies one helicopter and one aeroplane, while categories B to D fly two or three helicopter types and no aeroplane. Crew demand was derived from three operational rules. A prototype scheduling application models assignment, rotation and currency alerting. At the target scale of 182 pilots and 772 weekly slots it produces a complete roster in under half a second, with the staffing rate holding near 92 per cent. The model requires 151-182 pilots, most flying one or two types, with multi-type currency confined to a small senior pool. Rotation maintains proficiency and yields potential recurrent-training savings on the order of 8 to 22 million PLN per year. H1 holds. Multi-type operation is feasible when confined to a flexible pool and governed by an FRMS.

title: Short-Term Effects of the 12 p.m. Rule in Germany -A Difference-in-Differences Approach
affiliations: Helmut-Schmidt-Universität/ Universität der Bundeswehr Hamburg and University of the Federal Armed Forces Hamburg - Department of Economics

detail.title: Short-Term Effects of the 12 p.m. Rule in Germany -A Difference-in-Differences Approach
detail.abstract: Strong increases and intraday fluctuations in fuel prices have intensified political debates about competition and market power in retail fuel markets for some time now. In response to rising fuel prices following the disruption of global oil supply chains in 2026, Germany introduced among other regulations the so-called 12 p.m. rule in April 2026. Under this regulation, filling stations are only allowed to increase fuel prices once per day at 12 p.m., while price reductions remain possible at any time. Utilizing a high-frequency Difference-inDifferences approach with France as a control group, this paper analyzes the short-term effects of this regulation. Our baseline results indicate that the regulation reduced German gasoline prices by approximately 1 to 2 cents per liter in the short run. Furthermore, we find regional heterogeneity driven by local supply structures, border distance and thus competitive dynamics. However, due to the relatively short post-treatment period, no conclusions regarding long-term effects can be drawn yet.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents Part B of the Need Engineering Framework — the applied methodology for practitioners seeking to identify latent needs, validate commercial opportunities, design products that progress through the six stages of the Need Formation Sequence, and build recurrence architecture into their business model. Part B is designed to stand alone and be used independently, while serving as the direct applied counterpart to Part A, which establishes the formal theoretical foundation.

The paper introduces four Digital Need Observation Methods — search query analysis, complaint and forum mining, workaround identification, and behavioral trace reading — each representing a digital equivalent of an established qualitative research approach, adapted for the environment in which behavioral evidence now predominantly resides. These methods operationalise the Behavioral Signal Axiom of Part A, which establishes that observed behavior provides more reliable evidence of genuine need than stated preference. 

Part B further provides the Need Map template for structuring identified needs into commercial decisions, the Three-Variable Entry Scoring Framework for validating market entry positions, a stage-by-stage design guide for moving users through the Need Formation Sequence from exposure to dependency, a recurrence architecture system grounded in the Recurrence Theorem, and the Need Engineering Audit — a diagnostic instrument for identifying where a product has stalled and what structural changes are required.

The methodology draws on behavioral economics, consumer psychology, and entrepreneurship research, while contributing an original synthesis adapted for practitioners in resource-constrained environments including emerging markets. The Need Engineering Framework was first presented publicly on January 25, 2026, at the Founders Lab event in Lagos, Nigeria. Part A — SSRN 6737599 — is available as a separate working paper.

title: Doing Good and Doing Well: The Rise of Prosocial Managers
affiliations: University of Pittsburgh - Katz Graduate School of Business, University of Washington - Michael G. Foster School of Business, California State University, Fullerton and

detail.title: Doing Good and Doing Well: The Rise of Prosocial Managers
detail.abstract: This paper examines how individuals’ prosocial tendency, proxied by involvement with charitable organizations, relates to career outcomes. We find that, compared with their non-prosocial counterparts, prosocial individuals are more likely to attain top executive positions, including non-CEO and CEO roles, and reach these positions more quickly. Cross-sectional evidence further shows that the results are stronger when i) the charitable organizations with which managers are involved are directly aimed at improving the welfare of others, consistent with prosocial tendency rather than general ability or energy driving the results; and ii) managers are promoted internally rather than hired externally, consistent with prosocial behavior fostering trust and goodwill within firms. Conditional on being in office, prosocial CEOs are less likely to be dismissed for poor performance. We also find that prosocial managers receive higher compensation than non-prosocial managers, partly because they are more likely to become CEOs and to lead larger and better-performing firms. Our findings suggest that prosocial tendency benefits individuals’ careers.

title: Stated and Revealed Preferences for AI-Generated Content
affiliations: University of Michigan Ross School of Business, UCLA Anderson and University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: Stated and Revealed Preferences for AI-Generated Content
detail.abstract: As AI-generated content proliferates on social media, the rise of terms like "AI slop" suggests viewers are averse to this content. We study whether this stated aversion translates into revealed preferences using a large-scale dataset of YouTube videos and comments, supplemented by an online experiment. We document that both the prevalence and negativity of comments mentioning AI in YouTube videos have risen over time. Exploiting within-video variation in when an AI mention first enters a video's top comments, we find that the appearance of an AI mention reduces views by 10% on average. The effect exists for short and long-form videos and is concentrated in smaller channels. An online experiment, which holds video content fixed and randomly varies AI disclosure at the selection and viewing stages, confirms these effects. Labeling a video as AI reduces selection probability by 23%, and exposure to an AI callout during viewing reduces watch time by 14% and lowers willingness to engage further with the creator's other videos.

title: The Three-dimensional Brand Perspective

detail.title: The Three-dimensional Brand Perspective
detail.abstract: The article develops the three-dimensional brand perspective as an analytical framework for describing the subject area of branding from the perspective of marketing and branding professionals. The starting point is that the brand cannot be understood solely as the company's strategic property, as the consumer's mental representation or as a cultural sign. Rather, it should be analysed in the intersection between the company's attempts at management, the consumer's formation of meaning and the cultural and societal discourses in which the brand circulates. The framework is not used as a new allexplanatory branding theory, but as an orientation tool that can qualify the choice of theory and level of analysis. Based on (Heding et al., 2020), it is shown how their eight branding approaches can be linked to economic, identity-based, consumer-based, relational, community-oriented, cultural and sensory theories, respectively. The article argues that the strength of the model lies in its ability to clarify the type of brand problem a given case raises. At the same time, a significant limitation is pointed out: If all dimensions are activated uncritically, the analysis risks becoming broader than it is precise.

title: The AI-Substitution Paradox: Formation Debt and the Consumption of Future Agency in the AGI Transition
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The AI-Substitution Paradox: Formation Debt and the Consumption of Future Agency in the AGI Transition
detail.abstract: Conventional economic indicators are lagging by design. They register structural deterioration only after it has become crisis. This article develops the AI-Substitution Paradox, the condition in which artificial intelligence raises present output while eroding the conditions under which long-horizon human action remains possible, and argues that the transition to artificial general intelligence intensifies rather than resolves it. The claim is conditional, not deterministic. The framework distinguishes scaffolded augmentation, in which AI strengthens human formation, from formative substitution, in which AI displaces the practice through which judgment is built. It specifies the institutional conditions under which erosion is predicted. At the centre of the argument is Formation Debt: the accumulated deficit in independent judgment that arises when professionals are trained inside AI-mediated rather than formative environments. Formation Debt is theorised as a temporal externality, a Pigovian externality extended across generations, in which present transactions impose structural costs on future cohorts who cannot take part in the decisions that produce their inheritance. A three-stage Formation Cliff trajectory is specified, together with two diagnostic instruments by which the trajectory can be detected, or refuted, a decade before credential statistics register any change: the Dependency Gap test and the Entry-Level Formative Audit, the latter formalised as a Formative Substitution Index. The article then traces how artificial general intelligence would amplify the paradox across the structural pillars of agency continuity (human capital formation, cognitive infrastructure, demographic renewal, fiscal governance, and institutional deliberation), and positions the Providence Value Unit, a composite continuity function over ten structural pillars, as the measurement architecture the AGI transition requires. Throughout, AGI functions as an acceleration scenario rather than a premise; the framework is stated, and falsifiable, under present-deployment AI. Pre-registered propositions testable within the coming decade expose it to disconfirmation. The central claim is diagnostic rather than prescriptive. Capability may rise while temporal credibility falls, and futures-oriented governance must be able to see that transaction while it is still occurring.

detail.abstract:
Purpose
This study aims to explore the interactions between older adults and socially assistive robot (SAR) in tourism retirement communities from the perspective of mobility, analyzing their acceptance of SAR and the impact on their well-being, in order to provide theoretical foundations and practical guidance for the technological empowerment of the residential tourism model.

Design/methodology/approach
This study employs experimental design with two separate studies involving older adults aged 45 to 75 who have experience with travel care. Study 1 includes 97 participants divided into two groups to examine the impact of task types (information vs emotional support) provided by artificial intelligence robots on the Satisfaction with Elderly Life. Study 2 expands to four groups with 155 participants to investigate the moderating effect of care models (family-based vs travel-based) and the mediating role of emotional connection in this relationship.

Findings
The experimental results indicate that the use of SAR, as an emerging artificial intelligence technology, significantly enhances the Satisfaction with Elderly Life of older adults in residential tourism by providing emotional support and facilitating social interaction (p < 0.01). Further analysis reveals that in the context of residential tourism, emotional support provided by SAR is more effective than informational support in home-based care situations, while no significant differences exist in group travel environments. Emotional connection plays a mediating role in these effects.

Originality/value
This study approaches the integration of SAR with the residential tourism model from a mobility perspective, exploring the potential and practical characteristics of technological empowerment in new elder care models, thereby addressing some of the existing research gaps. The findings suggest that SAR can effectively enhance the Satisfaction with Elderly Life and acceptance of older adults in residential tourism communities. This study not only enriches the research perspective on SAR in elder care but also provides technological support and theoretical basis for the practice of residential tourism, contributing to the broader goals of active aging and technologically supported care.

title: The Steeper Slope: Generative AI, the Junior Talent Pipeline, and the Self-Defeating Logic of Seniority-Biased Hiring

detail.title: The Steeper Slope: Generative AI, the Junior Talent Pipeline, and the Self-Defeating Logic of Seniority-Biased Hiring

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical position paper involving no human participants, patients, or personal data; therefore ethics approval and participant consent are not required.

detail.abstract: A claim has moved, in under three years, from individual practitioners to industry-wide policy: that generative AI has eliminated the need to hire and train junior knowledge workers, because a senior equipped with AI can absorb the work juniors once did. Firms are now acting on it. Large technology employers have cut new-graduate hiring by roughly half relative to pre-pandemic levels, and rm-level evidence documents a seniority-biased pattern in which junior employment falls at AI-adopting rms while senior employment holds steady. This paper argues that the inference behind these cuts is locally defensible but globally self-defeating, in three analytical steps. First, it synthesizes the experimental evidence showing that AI's productivity uplift is decreasing in prior skill and that AI compresses the time novices need to reach competencethe same mechanism, viewed two ways. Second, it formalizes these facts in an individual value-curve model in which the worker's learning rate is the decisive parameter. Thirdthe paper's main contributionit scales that model to the rm and then the labor market, representing the workforce as a stock-ow pipeline in which seniors are produced only by juniors who mature. The model shows that a no-junior policy raises capability briey and then erodes it; that the current stability of senior employment is a transient funded by the pre-2023 junior cohort; and that if many rms adopt the policy at once, the external senior market on which each is implicitly relying collapsesa coordination failure on a shared human-capital commons. I close with a decision framework specifying the three conditions under which hiring a junior dominates an AI-only conguration, and with falsiable predictions. The central result is that the current wave of junior-hiring cuts, insofar as it is rationalized by AI substitution, is a privately rational and collectively dangerous strategy.

title: The Decoupling of Productivity from Human Hands: Why AI Breaks the Abstraction Ladder
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Decoupling of Productivity from Human Hands: Why AI Breaks the Abstraction Ladder
detail.abstract: For two centuries the rebuttal to fears of technological unemployment has been that workers always find other work. They have, but only because each new technology, while automating one kind of task, left a complementary kind that only humans could do, into which displaced workers moved. This paper argues that AI removes that second condition. AI is general cognitive capability rather than a task-specific tool, so the new work it calls into being is work the same capability can perform good enough and cheaper: the comparative-advantage niche that every prior transition reopened does not reopen, and the returns accrue to compute, the scarce complementary asset, rather than to a new layer of human labour. The escape was never that new work appeared; it was that the new work was work only humans could do, and that is the condition this transition is the first to break. The argument is structural and holds whatever the new work turns out to be, because whatever it is, it is cognitive. What rose across past transitions, the absolute cognitive content of work, now falls: the one channel left open, in-person and relational work, is largely ejection from the ladder rather than a rung up it. A falsifiable forecast conditional on the capability trajectory, the account is a prerequisite for policy: reskilling, AI-capability regulation, and incremental welfare adjustment each presuppose an absorption mechanism it shows is no longer operating.

title: Determinants of Consumer Preference for Electric Scooters: Evidence from a Comparative Study of Ather and Hero
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and RIMT University

detail.title: Determinants of Consumer Preference for Electric Scooters: Evidence from a Comparative Study of Ather and Hero
detail.abstract: The Indian automobile industry is experiencing a significant transformation towards sustainable mobility, marked by a quick increase in the use of electric vehicles (EVs). The use of electric vehicles (EVs) is playing a crucial role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and decarbonizing India. Electric scooters, in particular, have become increasingly popular due to rising fuel costs, growing environmental concerns, and government support. This research study, titled "Determinants of Consumer Preference for Electric Scooters: Evidence from A Comparative Study of Ather and Hero", seeks to examine consumer purchasing behavior and compare two major companies in the Indian EV scooter market-Ather Energy and Hero MotoCorp, which includes the Vida electric scooters. Over the last two decades, the customer needs have been dynamically changing; hence, factors influencing customers' purchase decisions have varied. The study looks at important factors that affect consumer choices, such as price, battery performance, availability of charging facilities, brand reputation, design and features, and operating costs. The study also reveals that demographic factors, such as age and income, also plays an important role in shaping consumer preferences for two-wheeler EVs. Data was gathered through a structured questionnaire from a selected group of respondents, and it was analyzed using percentage calculations, tables, and visual representations. The results of the study show the level of consumer awareness, brand preferences, the perceived value of the products, and the satisfaction levels of users with both brands.

detail.abstract: Consumer social responsibility (CNSR) is a critical determinant influencing consumer's socially conscious purchasing behavior. This study operationalizes the concept of CNSR, empirically predicts consumers' inclination towards socially responsible products, and examines the impact of personal traits on consumers' preferences for such products. An exploratory sequential mixed-method approach is employed to validate the proposed sequential mediation model. Data were collected from 613 consumers who are aware of product social friendliness, and key results were further validated through two-round semi-structured interviews. The findings contribute to understanding the relationship between consumer personality traits, CNSR, and consumer purchasing behavior.

title: Impact of Social Media on Consumer buying Behavior among College Students

detail.title: Impact of Social Media on Consumer buying Behavior among College Students
detail.abstract: Social media has emerged as one of the most powerful forces shaping consumer behavior in the digital age. This study investigates the impact of social media platforms on the buying behavior of college students in India, with a specific focus on platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, and WhatsApp. Using a structured survey methodology, data was collected from 120 undergraduate college students across SR University, Warangal. The findings reveal that social media significantly influences product discovery, brand perception, and final purchase decisions. Influencer marketing and peer reviews were found to be the two most compelling factors driving purchasing intent. The study concludes that businesses targeting the youth demographic must invest in a strong social media presence and influencer-driven campaigns to remain competitive. Recommendations are offered for marketers and small business owners seeking to leverage social media effectively.

title: AI, Learning Content, and the Future Supply of Managers

detail.title: AI, Learning Content, and the Future Supply of Managers
detail.abstract: Generative AI automates the entry-level cognitive work through which firms train their managers. How does this affect the future supply of managers? Standard AI-exposure measures capture output exposure - the share of a job's tasks AI can do. I build an index of learning content - the skill that the worker builds by doing the work - from O*NET's ratings of work activities. In a panel of roughly 9,000 U.S. public firms (Revelio Labs, 2017-2024), headcount in exposed occupations falls 3.6% by 2024 relative to unexposed occupations within the same firm, and by 8.1% at the highest AI-capability firms, beginning in the quarter of ChatGPT's release. Among AI-capable firms, entry headcount falls 1.1% per standard deviation of learning content where poaching is high, with no effect where it is low and no such gradient for output exposure. This implies that AI is contracting on-the-job human-capital formation, which output exposure alone does not capture. The work that is being cut is the main route into management, yielding about three times as many managers per entrant as unexposed work. Because an entry worker takes years to become a manager, the consequence for the manager stock is deferred. The cohorts already missing imply a shortfall of around 1-2% even if hiring recovers; should the contraction persist, the deficit reaches about 9% over two decades.

detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed the production, dissemination, and utilization of knowledge. While contemporary AI systems increasingly rely on large-scale interactions with users, the economic value generated through expert contributions remains largely unrecognized. This paper examines the structural asymmetry between AI platform owners and highly qualified users who continuously enrich AI ecosystems through original theories, methodological innovations, empirical data, and interdisciplinary insights. Drawing upon knowledge economy theory, institutional economics, digital commons theory, and scholarship on data labor, the study proposes a conceptual framework for recognizing, evaluating, and rewarding intellectual contributions within generative AI ecosystems. A hierarchical model of intellectual value creation is introduced, along with the concept of the "AI Knowledge Contributor" as a new economic actor. The paper outlines institutional principles-transparency, reciprocity, and fair compensation-for building a more equitable knowledge economy in which collective intelligence emerges through a balanced human-AI partnership.

title:

A Missing Dimension in System Optimization

detail.title:
Future Capability Preservation 
A Missing Dimension in System Optimization

detail.abstract:
This paper started with an observation.
The more systems I examined, the more often I encountered the same pattern:
organizations, technologies, supply chains, and institutions improved according
to the metrics used to evaluate them, while some appeared to lose capabilities
that later became important.
The losses rarely appeared on dashboards or in performance reports. Most
became visible only after conditions changed.
This observation led to a question: modern systems are highly effective at mea-
suring what they gain, but how effective are they at measuring what they lose?
This paper explores the possibility that an important dimension of system qual-
ity remains underexamined. I refer to this dimension as Future Capability
Preservation.
Future capability is defined as the capacity of a system to preserve, generate, and
expand beneficial transformation opportunities under conditions of uncertainty.
The concept is related to resilience, sustainability, adaptability, and foresight,
but differs by focusing specifically on the possibility space that remains available
after optimization, improvement, or transformation has occurred.
The central argument is simple: a system’s long-term success depends not only
on what it achieves, but on what it remains capable of becoming.

title: The Authored Universe: Cognitive Sovereignty and the Symmetric Closure of Knowledge Asymmetry

detail.abstract: This article argues that the extraction of value through informational asymmetry, what the article formalizes as the Blaeu rent, is categorically distinct from Ricardian scarcity rents and Schumpeterian innovation rents: it scales with the counterparty's blindness, is invariant to productive merit, and is dissolved entirely by symmetric closure. The argument proceeds in three interlocking registers. The first is philosophical: drawing on Maurice Merleau-Ponty's account of motor intentionality, Martin Heidegger's analysis of the ready-to-hand, and Antonio Damasio's somatic-marker hypothesis, the article defends the existential claim that some intentional states carry content before they are verbalized, and that pre-articulate knowledge, alongside acquired, derived, received, and inherited knowledge, constitutes a legitimate and analytically distinct mode of knowledge entry. The second is formal: the article introduces a fiber bundle topology to represent semantically overloaded concepts without metric distortion; formalizes the Blaeu rent as a function of the information set differential between counterparties, subject to strict conditions of merit-invariance; presents a mechanism-design proof, grounded in adverse selection dynamics, demonstrating that institutional adoption of symmetric instruments is the dominant rational strategy for capital; and formalizes the irreversible loss of cognitive potential under asymmetric conditions as a cognitive entropy law, drawing on Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen's thermodynamic framework, showing that the waste is path-dependent and permanent. The third is architectural: the article specifies the federated, homomorphically encrypted governance structure required to make the sovereignty claim real rather than nominal, and addresses the warrant-adjudication problem through cryptographically verifiable zero-knowledge credential systems. The central finding is that symmetric closure of the information gap dissolves the Blaeu rent entirely while leaving earned competitive advantage, including first-mover position, execution capacity, and risk tolerance, wholly intact.

title: Future Prospects of Drone Delivery Services in the Food Delivery Industry of Punjab
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Future Prospects of Drone Delivery Services in the Food Delivery Industry of Punjab
detail.abstract: Drone delivery is becoming a major innovation in the logistics and food delivery sectors. This research project examines the future of drone delivery services in the food delivery industry in Punjab. The study explores technological progress, legal regulations, operational advantages and obstacles, and consumer perceptions of this new delivery method. The research uses a descriptive and exploratory methodology, drawing from both primary and secondary data. The results show that drone delivery has the potential to enhance the speed, efficiency, and reach of delivery services, particularly in urban and distant regions. Nevertheless, several challenges, including strict regulations, technical hurdles, and the need for proper infrastructure, continue to hinder its widespread use. With government support and ongoing technological improvements, drone delivery is likely to become a key part of Punjab's future logistics system.

title: IRON: Index of Robustness of Organizations facing Digital Dependency

detail.title: IRON: Index of Robustness of Organizations facing Digital Dependency

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently on the author's own resources.

detail.abstract:
When a digital service fails, the organizational impact depends on the service's resilience and, more decisively, on the organization's capacity to operate without it. This capacity — here termed robustness — is structurally absent from existing frameworks. ISO 27001, NIST CSF, ISO 22301, and DORA evaluate the means deployed to protect the information system, but none measures the organizational consequences of its failure. No existing framework crosses digital resilience with functional substitutability and business criticality.

This article introduces IRON (Index of Robustness of Organizations facing Digital Dependency), a composite index that evaluates each business process along three independent axes: functional substitutability (X), whether the process can continue without its digital service; digital resilience (Y), the capacity of the service to withstand a disruption; and business criticality (Z), the impact on organizational longevity if the process stops. The aggregated score, weighted by criticality, identifies where fragility concentrates and where improvement effort is most effective. IRON is sector-agnostic and designed to complement existing framework assessments by adding the dimension they structurally miss.

A three-phase validation strategy is proposed. Retrospective coherence testing on two documented incidents with contrasting outcomes shows that IRON scores are consistent with observed impacts. Empirical calibration through field pilots is the next step.

title: A Deterministic Accounting Event Adjudication Framework for Natural-Language Accounting Systems: Design, Principles, and Implementation in the PEAKUS Engine

detail.title: A Deterministic Accounting Event Adjudication Framework for Natural-Language Accounting Systems: Design, Principles, and Implementation in the PEAKUS Engine
detail.abstract:
The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence and natural language processing in accounting has created a critical tension. Rule-based systems are deterministic but rigid, failing on transactions outside predefined boundaries. Machine learning classifiers are flexible but probabilistic, producing confidence scores rather than auditable outcomes. Large language models are generative but non-deterministic, producing outputs that may vary across executions and may hallucinate information not present in the input. None of these approaches provides a principled, auditable, and deterministic path from natural-language transaction descriptions to accounting events. 

This study addresses this gap by proposing the Deterministic Accounting Event Adjudication (DAEA) Framework. The framework introduces an explicit adjudication layer positioned between semantic extraction and journal entry generation. It treats accounting-event determination as an independent problem that must be resolved before any journal entry is generated. 

The framework is governed by five principles—No Guessing, Uniqueness, Determinism, Rejection, and Extensibility—and operates on a semantic evidence model consisting of five core dimensions (Action, Object, State, Amount, and Payment). 

Operationalized through the PEAKUS Engine, the framework is evaluated using six representative case studies and a dataset of 1,594 natural-language transactions. Results provide empirical evidence of 100% deterministic consistency across repeated executions, zero false acceptances on ambiguous inputs, and approximately 95% adjudication coverage for well-formed transactions. 

The study makes five theoretical contributions: (1) deterministic adjudication as an alternative to probabilistic classification; (2) an evidence-centered model of accounting interpretation; (3) Action as the primary determinant of accounting-event identity; (4) rejection as a legitimate adjudication outcome; and (5) the distinction between Business Events and Accounting Events. The framework offers practical benefits in auditability, explainability, traceability, and human-in-the-loop integration.

detail.abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems have become fundamental components of modern organisations, enabling the integrated management of finance, human resources, procurement, customer relations, and operational processes. Leading platforms such as SAP S/4HANA and Oracle Fusion Cloud have advanced enterprise operations through cloud adoption, real-time analytics, and process standardisation. However, despite these advancements, contemporary ERP systems remain fundamentally process-centric, requiring users to navigate complex interfaces, interpret predefined workflows, and manually interact with multiple modules. Research consistently identifies user training burden, interaction complexity, and limited adaptability as persistent shortcomings of market-leading ERP solutions (AlMuhayfith and Shaiti, 2020; Garg and Khurana, 2017). Simultaneously, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and intelligent automation has introduced new opportunities for intent-driven, conversational enterprise architectures (Schnepf et al., 2024; Wornow et al., 2024). This paper argues that existing ERP systems have not fully leveraged AI as a primary interaction layer and continue to rely heavily on traditional workflow paradigms. Through a structured comparative analysis of SAP S/4HANA and Oracle Fusion Cloud against an AI-native design framework, this study identifies key architectural limitations and proposes an AI-native ERP model centred on intelligent workflow orchestration, conversational interaction, and autonomous task execution. The feasibility of this architecture is demonstrated through Trifusion Foundry, an AIpowered enterprise platform developed by the author, integrating HRMS, ITSM, role-based security, and intelligent workflow automation. It is acknowledged that, as both researcher and developer of Trifusion Foundry, a potential conflict of interest exists; the platform is therefore presented strictly as a proof-of-concept implementation rather than a comparative benchmark. Findings suggest that AI-native ERP architectures hold significant potential to reduce operational complexity, lower training dependency, and transform enterprise software from process-driven tools into intent-driven organisational platforms. This is a conceptual position paper: it advances and structures the architectural argument through analytical synthesis of existing literature, and explicitly identifies empirical validation, including controlled user studies and benchmark experiments, as essential future work rather than a contribution of this paper.

detail.title: Gated Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Inverse Local Volatility Calibration with Learned Regime Structure
detail.abstract: Local volatility calibration from discrete option prices is inherently ill-posed, and the classicalDupire formula fails catastrophically under realistic market conditions of noise and sparsity.Physics-Informed Neural Networks offer a principled alternative through PDE-constrainedlearning, but standard joint optimisation of price and volatility networks encounters a fourth-order gradient pathology that limits convergence quality. We propose a decoupled PINNarchitecture in which the call-price surface is learned under Black-Scholes constraints whilstvolatility is recovered via independent regression. A stop-gradient operation eliminates thegradient pathology by breaking the computational dependency of PDE residuals on volatilityparameters. This architectural choice yields a structural invariance: volatility error becomesindependent of the PDE loss weight λPDE , removing what is typically the most consequentialhyperparameter in such frameworks. Additionally, we represent volatility as a gated mixtureof two expert networks, enabling regime structure to emerge naturally during training. Themethod is validated on synthetic two-regime surfaces and real equity options, demonstratingsubstantial improvements in reconstruction stability under data sparsity compared to Dupire-based methods. No-arbitrage constraints are satisfied consistently throughout the calibrateddomain.

detail.abstract: Falling natural gas prices amid the shale boom triggered a sharp decline in U.S. coal production, with over half of Appalachian mines shuttering between 2011 and 2016. In this paper, we use administrative data on mine activity and employment to measure the impact of coal mine closures on local economic outcomes. Using difference-in-differences, we find these closures significantly increased local unemployment and reduced jobs, wages, and output. We estimate a job loss multiplier of 2.0—substantially higher than in previous busts—likely driven by a rising local wage premium that amplified the impact of each lost mining job on the broader regional economy.
